title: Torsion-free counit-computing resolutions for reduction of towers
statement: Let l be prime, T a scheme and r any Reduction T (Rrings l T) [def-sp-tower-class-reduction, def-sp-tower-class-coefficients]. For every cochain complex K of abelian towers [def-sp-tower-class-systems], there exist P and a quasi-isomorphism q:P → K such that multiplication by l^(n+1) is monic on the level-n sheaf of P^i for every integer i and natural n, and the actual universal-derived counit r.model.epsilon at P is an isomorphism. No quotient exactness, distinguished triangle, units object, or derived-adjunction-unit formula is asserted.

source.place: Functorial derived completion: simultaneous tensor with quotient rings; resolution [Z --ell^n--> Z] with transitions (ell,1). For the ordinary quotient see Stacks sites-modules.tex, lemma-adjointness-tensor-restrict (03D7); for resolutions see sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-K-flat-resolution (06YS) and lemma-derived-base-change (06YY).

proof.text: For each abelian sheaf X, sheafify the free abelian presheaf on its sections. Its evaluation map is epic because the presheaf evaluation is sectionwise surjective; all its nonzero integer multiples are monic because free abelian groups are torsion free and sheafification is exact. Apply this construction levelwise to towers. For a complex K form the disk cover C^i = F(K^i) ⊕ F(K^(i-1)), with differential (x,y) ↦ (0,x) and augmentation ε(x)+dε(y). The naturality of evaluation proves the chain-map identity and the first summand proves degreewise epimorphy.

Let A be the kernel of the disk-cover augmentation C → K. The canonical map Cone(A → C) → K is a quasi-isomorphism by the short-exact cone comparison. Nonzero integer multiplication is monic on C^i, on its subobject A^i, and on their binary biproducts, hence on every term of this cone. Exact level evaluation sends these monomorphisms to the asserted ones; primality ensures l^(n+1) is nonzero.

On every complex P with levelwise monic l^(n+1), apply the ordinary-cokernel theorem term by term to obtain the short exact sequence from the power-twisted P to P to the forgotten ordinary reduction of P. A quasi-isomorphism between two such P induces a morphism of these short exact sequences. Power-transition twisting preserves quasi-isomorphisms. The long exact homology sequence therefore makes its forgotten reduction a quasi-isomorphism. The supplied Forget is faithful by its section-map prescription; since it is exact it detects quasi-isomorphisms. Thus ordinary reduction preserves quasi-isomorphisms between these regular complexes.

Apply the resolving-class theorem to ordinary reduction followed by localization on the homotopy category, using the resolutions and invariance just proved. Precomposition with the full essentially-surjective homotopy quotient preserves the defining pointwise Kan extension: the induced structured-arrow functor is full, essentially surjective and hence initial. Transport along the canonical quotient/localization comparisons. This yields a universal cochain derived pair whose counit is invertible on each regular P. The canonical counit-compatible isomorphism between universal pairs identifies it with the supplied r.model pair, so r.model.epsilon.app P is invertible. Combine this with the constructed resolution.

from.place: variable-power coefficient resolution in simultaneous Kummer reduction

lean.statement:
theorem powerSystem_acyclic_resolution (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (T : Scheme.{u})
    (r : Reduction T (Rrings l T)) (K : CochainComplex (Ab T) ℤ) :
    ∃ (P : CochainComplex (Ab T) ℤ) (q : P ⟶ K),
      QuasiIso q ∧ (∀ (i : ℤ) (n : ℕ),
        Mono (l ^ (n + 1) • 𝟙 ((P.X i).obj (op n)))) ∧
      IsIso (r.model.epsilon.app P)
